introduction: This level targets the analysis of pin-jointed frames (Trusses). Examiners frequently test the 'Perfect Truss' formula and your visual ability to identify members carrying zero force without doing any calculations.

core_concepts.title: The Perfect Truss
core_concepts.description:
A truss that has exactly enough members to retain its shape under load without collapsing. 
Formula: **$m = 2j - 3$** 
Where $m$ = number of members, $j$ = number of joints. 
If $m < 2j - 3$, it is a Deficient truss. If $m > 2j - 3$, it is a Redundant truss.

core_concepts.title: Zero-Force Member: Rule 1
core_concepts.description: If exactly **two members** meet at an unloaded joint, and the members are NOT in a straight line (non-collinear), then **the force in both members is zero**.

core_concepts.title: Zero-Force Member: Rule 2
core_concepts.description: If exactly **three members** meet at an unloaded joint, and two of those members are in a straight line (collinear), then **the force in the third (non-collinear) member is strictly zero**.

important_entities.name: Method of Joints
important_entities.significance: When analyzing a truss mathematically, the 'Method of Joints' can only be applied at a joint where there are **no more than two unknown member forces**. If there are 3 unknowns, you must use the Method of Sections.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: A fundamental assumption in truss analysis is that members do NOT carry bending moments or shear forces. Truss members carry **Axial Forces ONLY**—they are either strictly in Tension or strictly in Compression.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Lock this rhythm into your head: $m = 2j - 3$. Anything less is deficient.

exam_strategy_tips: A favorite GATE and State AE visual question: A T-shaped joint is given where 3 members meet with no external load. What is the force in the vertical stem of the 'T'? Answer: By Rule 2, it is 0 (Zero).
